summary: Mostly not. On BTC, ETH and SOL, Momentum(10) crossing 0, or staying above or below it, did the same as random entries on 1h and 4h. The result that holds up is the 1h cross up through its 90th percentile, at 0.19% ahead of random after 20 candles. Those crosses fire in volatile candles, so the gain reflects when they fire, not which way price went.

verdicts.use: Buying a spike (cross up through the 90th percentile)
verdicts.text: Beat random on 1h by 0.19% after 20 candles, mostly in downtrends. These crosses fire in volatile candles in a window that rose, so price moved more after them, which says nothing about direction.

notes: On 1h, Momentum(10) crossing up through 0 gave 12,610 entries in 2,500 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.04% ahead of random entries, inside the luck band. The short on the cross down through 0 landed in the same place, and so did both crosses on 4h. Holding a long while above 0 on 1h enters about six and a half times as often as the cross, and it also did the same as random.

On 1h, the cross up through its 90th percentile beat random by 0.19% after 20 candles. It held without its strongest stretch, Feb 17–19, 2021, and showed at 10 candles but not at 50 or 100. The gain sits in downtrends: 0.28% ahead when the pair was below its 200-day SMA, and the same as random above it. On ETH it rests on signals on Feb 24–25, 2026.

This cross fires mostly in volatile candles. The luck band keeps the signals' timing but not that volatility, so in a window that rose, bigger moves after those candles can beat random for longs without picking a direction. On daily the same cross beat random by 4.87%, but only because of 5 entries between Jul 31 and Aug 27, 2021. SOL's 9.81% rests on that same stretch.

On daily, shorting while Momentum(10) was below 0 beat random by 2.1% after 20 days and held without its strongest stretch. In uptrends it beat random by 3.45%, but only because of entries between Nov 13, 2021 and Jan 19, 2022. In downtrends it did the same as random. Going long while above 0 also beat random on daily, which a setting that read direction could not do on both sides, and it rests on only 30 separate moves.

On daily, the cross up through 0 did 2.16% worse than random, but only because of signals between Sep 5 and Oct 28, 2022. SOL alone was 5.11% worse, from the same stretch. The cross down through 0 did the same as random pooled. In uptrends, shorts on that cross beat random by 2.92%, held without their strongest stretch and showed at 10, 20 and 50 days. In downtrends that short showed nothing.

For a long DCA bot on 1h or 4h, a cross of 0 timed entries no better than random, so the take profit and DCA orders carry the result. Leave it out of the start condition, or keep it only as a filter beside other conditions. The 1h cross up through the 90th percentile marks candles after which price moved further. That fits a wider take profit or DCA spacing better than a direction filter. On daily, the short results showed only above the 200-day SMA, so test them on your own pair before you use them as a filter.
